html:
A deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh's international airport, killing 12 people and injuring hundreds, has drawn global condemnation and prompted Donald Trump to evaluate whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Yemeni rebels, intensifying regional tensions amidst an ongoing "Iran war."

Middle East Security: The Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport suspended operations and resulted in 12 fatalities, including four Saudi citizens, a US citizen, and other foreign nationals, with over 300 injured. Donald Trump condemned the "terrible" attack and is weighing military support for Saudi Arabia, while the incident follows other recent strikes on Saudi airports and oil infrastructure. An Israeli official indicated no proactive Israeli strike would occur before upcoming elections to maintain stable oil prices. In the Gulf, a second oil tanker caught fire within 48 hours in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's IRGC claiming it struck a naval mine, raising questions about changing rules of engagement.

Great Power Dynamics: Amidst ongoing conflict, Trump has called for Ukraine to get a new leader, criticizing Volodymyr Zelensky for high diesel prices in the US and suggesting he has not done enough to end the war. This follows a US-Russia diesel deal to release fuel into the US, which Zelensky condemned, stating it would help Moscow fund the war. Russia subsequently launched a glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia, killing at least 20 people including children, which Zelensky linked to Russia expressing "thanks" for the diesel deal. Russia's Vladimir Putin also informed Trump of stalled peace negotiations with Ukraine amidst mutual military escalation.

International Law & Human Rights: South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong defense of human rights and international law. Hours after the announcement, the US imposed new sanctions on the International Criminal Court, with Nobel Peace laureate Pillay calling the sanctions "unacceptable." Trump expressed anger at not receiving the prize, claiming he ended wars and freed all Israeli hostages, and criticized Norway for the decision, calling Pillay unknown "except for her hatred of Israel."

Regional Unrest & Humanitarian Concerns: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections until September 2027 and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation. Hamas and others criticized the postponement as a "political crime." One year after a US-brokered ceasefire in Gaza that saw Hamas release Israeli hostages, Palestinians describe the period as a "ceasefire in name only," with a child among eight killed by Israel on the anniversary. Separately, young men in Myanmar live in fear of being forcibly recruited into the army amidst a war of attrition against ethnic militias.

US Domestic Issues: Hurricane Isaias made landfall on Florida's panhandle as a Category 2 storm, weakening to a post-tropical cyclone after causing at least four deaths and leaving hundreds of thousands without power across the US. Additionally, two mass shootings occurred in the US: five people were killed in an apparent murder-suicide in Georgia, and eight people, including a pregnant woman and children, died in Pennsylvania before the suspect killed himself.
